mainTopic: Differences between a regular day and יום כיפור in the מקדש: the gold coal pan, the קטורת, the ramp, washing, and the wood piles on the מזבח
overview: This amud finishes the list of the kinds of gold. רב אשי then says there are really five kinds, each with a regular and a better grade, and a ברייתא confirms that the יום כיפור vessel was red זהב פרוים. Next the גמרא goes through the משנה's list of ways יום כיפור differs from a regular day. On יום כיפור the קטורת is ground extra-fine, and a ברייתא learns this from an extra word in the פסוק. On a regular day the כהנים go up the east side of the כבש because every turn must be to the right. On יום כיפור they walk up the middle, and the כהן גדול washes from a golden flask, both out of honor for the כהן גדול. A ברייתא then brings three views on how many wood piles were on the מזבח: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, and רבי מאיר, whose count matches the משנה. The גמרא traces each pile to its source in the פסוקים, and the ברייתא about the leftover limbs and fats continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the list of the kinds of gold
steps.stepSummary: The list of gold types (רב חסדא's list, begun on the previous amud) continues. It explains the names זהב מופז, זהב שחוט, זהב סגור and זהב פרוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [זהב מופז is called that] because it looks like פז (pearls). זהב שחוט is gold that can be spun like a thread. זהב סגור is called that because when a shop that sells it opens, all the other shops close. זהב פרוים is called that because it looks like the blood of bulls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a list that explains the names of different kinds of gold. This amud picks up the explanation partway through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name gets a short explanation based on what the word sounds like. שחוט is read as 'spun like a חוט.' סגור means 'closing,' because no one buys other gold once this gold is for sale. פרוים is linked to פרים, because it is red like bull's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A shining precious material (pearls), the basis of the name זהב מופז
A kind of gold; read here as 'spun like a thread'
'Closed' gold, the gold that makes other shops close
A reddish gold, compared to the blood of bulls (פָּרִים)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'שדומה לפז' finish the explanation of זהב מופז, which began on the previous lines.

phrases.english: because it resembles paz (pearls).
phrases.notes: Explains the name זהב מופז

phrases.english: Shachut gold — because it is spun like a thread.
phrases.notes: A play on words: שחוט is read as שנטוה כחוט, 'spun like a thread.'

phrases.english: Closed gold — because when it is opened (offered for sale),
all the other shops close.
phrases.notes: No one wants to buy any other gold

phrases.english: Parvayim gold — because it resembles the blood of bulls.
phrases.notes: פרוים is linked to פרים

steps.triggerLanguage: זָהָב שָׁחוּט — שֶׁנִּטְוֶה כְּחוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of gold types that began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each name for a kind of gold describes a feature of that gold: its shine, how easily it can be worked, its value, or its color.

steps.title: רב אשי says there are only five kinds of gold
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there are only five kinds of gold. Each kind comes in two grades: regular זהב and better זהב טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There are five kinds. Each one of them comes as regular gold and as 'good gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different way to count the kinds of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier list, 'זהב' and 'זהב טוב' were counted as two separate kinds. רב אשי says they are not kinds of their own. Instead, they are two grades that exist within each of the other five kinds.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: There are five,
and each and every one has in it
gold and good gold.
phrases.notes: Two grades within each kind

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: חֲמִשָּׁה הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way of counting the list from Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are five kinds of gold. 'זהב' and 'זהב טוב' are grades within each kind, not separate kinds.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that the יום כיפור gold was red זהב פרוים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that on a regular day the gold of the vessel was greenish, but on יום כיפור it was red. That red gold is זהב פרוים, which looks like bull's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: Every day its gold was greenish, but today it was red. And that is זהב פרוים, which looks like the blood of bulls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support, using the phrase 'תניא נמי הכי' ('it was also taught this way').
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that זהב פרוים is a red gold, like bull's blood. It also shows that gold came in different grades and colors. On a regular day the vessel was greenish gold, and on יום כיפור it was the finer red gold.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way': a ברייתא is brought as support
'And this is…', which identifies one thing with another

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
Every day its gold was greenish,
but today (Yom Kippur) it was red —
and this is parvayim gold
which resembles the blood of bulls.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the explanation of זהב פרוים and for the idea of grades within gold
steps.raayaObject: That זהב פרוים is red like bull's blood, and that gold comes in different grades
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the gold vessel on a regular day compared with יום כיפור
steps.whatToRemember: On יום כיפור the vessel was made of the finest red gold, זהב פרוים. On regular days it was greenish gold.

steps.title: The משנה's next differences: the amount and fineness of the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next lines of the משנה. Every day a פרס of קטורת is offered in the morning. On a regular day the קטורת is fine, and on יום כיפור it is extra-fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day he offers a פרס in the morning, and so on. Every day it was fine, and today it was extra-fine (fine from the fine).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next point. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step, which gives the source for this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה keeps listing the differences between a regular day and יום כיפור. Here the difference is how finely the קטורת is ground. The 'וכו׳' means the quote is shortened, and the rest of that line is about the amount of קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a מָנֶה, the amount of קטורת offered each time
Extra-fine, finer than the normal fine

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם מַקְרִיב פְּרָס שַׁחֲרִית וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Every day he offers a peras in the morning, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Every day it (the incense) was fine,
but today it is the finest of the fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם מַקְרִיב פְּרָס שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה to start a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום כיפור the קטורת must be ground extra-fine.

steps.title: Why does the verse need to say 'fine'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק about יום כיפור says 'דקה' (fine), since another פסוק already says the קטורת must be ground fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Why does the פסוק say 'דקה' (fine)? Doesn't it already say 'And you shall grind some of it finely'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the word 'דקה' in the יום כיפור section is needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות already requires all קטורת to be ground fine. So the extra word in the פסוק about יום כיפור seems unnecessary. The ברייתא assumes the Torah has no extra words, so this word must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why does the verse need to say this?'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Fine" — why does the verse say it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יב

phrases.english: Has it not already been stated:
"And you shall grind some of it finely"!
phrases.notes: שמות ל:לו

steps.triggerLanguage: ״דַּקָּה״ מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'דקה' in the פסוק about יום כיפור teaches

steps.title: The extra word teaches 'extra-fine'
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'דקה' teaches that on יום כיפור the קטורת must be finer than the normal fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to include 'fine from the fine' (extra-fine).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question: the extra word teaches the rule of 'extra-fine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since regular fineness is already required by the פסוק in שמות, the second mention must add a higher level. This gives the משנה's rule a source in the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra word 'דקה' in the יום כיפור section is the source that the קטורת on that day must be extra-fine.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to include the finest of the fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְהָבִיא דַּקָּה מִן הַדַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word teaches that the קטורת of יום כיפור must be extra-fine.

steps.title: The משנה: priests normally go up the eastern side of the ramp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: every day the כהנים go up on the eastern side of the כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the כהנים go up on the eastern side of the ramp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next difference in the משנה. This sets up the next step, which explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us which side of the altar's ramp the כהנים use to go up on a regular day. The משנה's point is that the כהן גדול does it differently on יום כיפור. The גמרא now explains why the regular practice is to use the east side.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: Every day the priests ascend
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: on the eastern side of the ramp.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֲנִים עוֹלִין בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל כֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה to start a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a regular day the כהנים go up the eastern side of the כבש.

steps.title: The reason: every turn must be to the right
steps.stepSummary: The reason is a general rule: every turn you make in the מקדש must be to the right. When a כהן reaches the top of the ramp, a right turn brings him to the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: All the turns that you turn should only be to the right, toward the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's rule by quoting a general principle with the words 'דאמר מר' ('as the Master said').
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ramp is on the south side of the מזבח. A כהן who goes up and turns right ends up facing east. That is why he goes up on the eastern side of the ramp. The rule about the eastern side is just one result of the general rule to always turn right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As the Master said': quotes an accepted teaching
By way of the right, turning to the right

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of always turning to the right shapes how the כהנים move all through the מקדש, not only on the ramp.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים go up on the east side because every turn in the עבודה must be to the right, and at the top of the ramp a right turn leads east.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
All the turns that you turn

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: should be only by way of the right, toward the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: כׇּל פִּינּוֹת שֶׁאַתָּה פּוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the משנה's rule in Step 7
steps.raayaObject: Why the כהנים go up on the eastern side of the כבש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general teaching that every turn must be to the right

steps.title: On יום כיפור they go up and down the ramp in the middle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on יום כיפור the כהנים go up and come down the middle of the כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But today (on יום כיפור) they go up in the middle and come down in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It sets up a contrast with step 7, where on a regular day the כהנים went up on the eastern side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day the כהנים walk up the side of the ramp and turn right. On יום כיפור the rule changes, and they walk straight up and down the center. The next step gives the reason.

phrases.english: But today they go up in the middle
phrases.notes: 'Today' means יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and come down in the middle.
phrases.notes: Different from a regular day (step 7), when they went up on the east side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹם (עוֹלִין) בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the יום כיפור contrast to the regular-day rule in steps 7–8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום כיפור the כהנים go up and down the middle of the כבש.

steps.title: The reason for walking in the middle is honor for the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, and answers that the כהן גדול walks in the middle because it is more honorable for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because of the honor of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule in step 9 and answers right away: the change is out of respect for the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking along the side is less important. Since the כהן גדול does the עבודה on יום כיפור, he walks in the center as a mark of honor. The regular 'turn right' rule from step 8 gives way to his honor on this day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because of the honor of the High Priest.
phrases.notes: It is more honorable to walk in the center than along the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rule quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Why on יום כיפור the כהנים walk in the middle of the ramp
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle of honoring the כהן גדול

steps.title: On a regular day the כהן גדול washes from the כיור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: every day the כהן גדול washes his hands and feet from the כיור, like everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the כהן גדול washes his hands and feet from the כיור, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It sets up the next question about why יום כיפור is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' (וכו׳) points to the rest of the משנה. It says that on יום כיפור the כהן גדול washes from a special golden flask (קיתון של זהב) instead of the כיור. So the change on יום כיפור is where he washes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Washes (sanctifies) his hands and feet before the עבודה
The laver, the large copper washbasin in the courtyard
Etc., meaning the rest of the line continues

phrases.english: Every day the High Priest
sanctifies his hands and his feet
from the laver, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: on יום כיפור he washes from a golden flask.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֵן [גָּדוֹל] מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו מִן הַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, a new detail of the day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every day the כהן גדול washes from the כיור. On יום כיפור he washes from a golden flask.

steps.title: The golden flask is also for the כהן גדול's honor
steps.stepSummary: Using the same question and the same answer, the גמרא explains that the golden flask on יום כיפור is out of honor for the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because of the honor of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the כהן גדול washes from a golden flask on יום כיפור, and gives the same answer as before: his honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the reason from step 10 for a new rule. Washing from a fancy golden vessel instead of the shared כיור honors the כהן גדול on his special day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because of the honor of the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for step 11's rule, the same reason as in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: Why the כהן גדול washes from a golden flask on יום כיפור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The principle of honoring the כהן גדול

steps.title: On a regular day there were four wood piles on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: every day there were four מערכות of wood on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day there were four arrangements (of wood) there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about the wood piles on the מזבח. It sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says four piles on a regular day, which implies five on יום כיפור. A מערכה is a separate stack of burning wood, each with its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrangements, meaning piles of wood burning on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the משנה's numbers in mind: four on a regular day and five on יום כיפור. The ברייתא that follows gives three opinions. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי give smaller numbers, but רבי מאיר's count (four and five) matches the משנה.

phrases.english: Every day there were there
four arrangements (of wood).
phrases.notes: On יום כיפור, five.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבַּע מַעֲרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every day there were four wood piles on the מזבח (five on יום כיפור).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: two piles every day, three on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה's view: two מערכות on a regular day and three on יום כיפור, and it lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Every day there were two piles, and today (יום כיפור) three. One is the big pile, one is the second pile for the קטורת, and one is the pile added on that day. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different count of the wood piles, starting with רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a regular day has only two piles. The big one burns the קרבנות, and the second one supplies coals for the קטורת. On יום כיפור a third pile is added to supply coals for the קטורת brought inside the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The large pile, where the קרבנות burn
The second pile, which supplies coals for the קטורת
The one added on that day (יום כיפור)
The תנא who holds two piles normally and three on יום כיפור

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Every day there were two arrangements,
and today, three.
One, the large arrangement;
and one, the second arrangement for the incense;
and one that they add on that day,
phrases.notes: For the קטורת of the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ שְׁתַּיִם מַעֲרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the topic of the משנה line in step 13, with a smaller count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: two piles every day (the large one and the קטורת one), three on יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: three piles every day, four on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds a pile for keeping the fire going: three on a regular day and four on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Every day three, and today four. One is the big pile, one is the second pile for the קטורת, one is for keeping the fire going, and one is the pile added on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's opinion, which disagrees with רבי יהודה by adding one more pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי agrees with all of רבי יהודה's piles. He adds a pile for קיום האש, kept ready so that if the big fire dies down, wood can be taken from it to keep the fire burning. So his numbers are one higher on both days.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds three piles normally and four on יום כיפור
Keeping the fire going, a backup pile to feed the main fire

steps.whatToRemember: Count of wood piles: רבי יהודה says 2 (regular) and 3 (יום כיפור). רבי יוסי adds a fire-maintenance pile, so 3 and 4. The משנה says 4 and 5, which is the view רבי מאיר gives in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Every day three, and today four.
One, the large arrangement;
and one, the second arrangement for the incense;
and one for the upkeep of the fire;
phrases.notes: This is the pile רבי יוסי adds.

phrases.english: and one that they add on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם שָׁלֹשׁ, וְהַיּוֹם אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: three piles every day (adding קיום האש), four on יום כיפור.

steps.title: A third view: four piles every day, five on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds there were four מערכות every day and five on יום כיפור, and lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: every day there were four piles, and on this day (יום כיפור) five. One is the big pile. One is the second pile, for the קטורת. One is for keeping the fire going. One is for the limbs and fats that did not finish burning from the evening before. And one is the extra pile they add on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third opinion on how many wood piles were on the מזבח. רבי מאיר adds a fourth daily pile, used to finish burning leftover limbs and fats from the night before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה counted two piles (three on יום כיפור). רבי יוסי added קיום האש (three, and four on יום כיפור). רבי מאיר adds one more pile for leftover אברים ופדרים, so he has four, and five on יום כיפור. In every view, the extra pile on יום כיפור is for the קטורת that is brought into the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The big main pile where the קרבנות were burned
The second pile, which supplied coals for the קטורת
Keeping the fire going (a backup pile)
Limbs and fats of the קרבנות

phrases.english: Rabbi (Meir) says:
phrases.notes: The usual printed גמרא says רבי מאיר here, but some versions leave out the name in round brackets and just say רבי.

phrases.english: Every day four, and on this day five.
One is the large pile,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁל מַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קְטוֹרֶת,
phrases.english: and one is the second pile, for the incense,
and one is for keeping the fire going,
and one is for limbs and fats
that were not burned up from the evening before,
and one that they add on that day.
phrases.notes: This is the extra pile for the יום כיפור קטורת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי (מֵאִיר) אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם אַרְבַּע, וְהַיּוֹם חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and highest count to the views of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. This count matches the משנה in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: four piles daily and five on יום כיפור, adding a pile for unburned limbs and fats.

steps.title: Where do the two piles everyone agrees on come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that all opinions have at least two piles and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone at least has two piles. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts looking for the sources of the piles. It begins with the two piles that every opinion agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three תנאים disagree about the extra piles, but nobody disagrees about the big pile and the קטורת pile. So the גמרא first secures the shared base before turning to the disputed piles.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: According to everyone, at any rate,
they all have two;
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת תַּרְתֵּי אִית לְהוּ, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing the opinions to asking for their scriptural sources.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source for the two piles that everyone agrees on.

steps.title: One verse teaches both basic piles
steps.stepSummary: ויקרא ו:ב teaches the big pile ('על מוקדה') and the קטורת pile ('ואש המזבח תוקד בו').
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'It is the עולה on its burning place on the מזבח all night.' That is the big pile. 'And the fire of the מזבח shall be kept burning on it.' That is the second pile, for the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading two parts of one verse. Each part teaches a separate pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the verse speaks about burning the עולה, so it means the big pile. The words 'ואש המזבח' mention fire again, and this extra mention is read as a second fire: the pile used for the קטורת.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"It is the burnt-offering on its flame
on the altar all night" (Leviticus 6:2) —
this is the large pile.
"And the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it" —
this is the second pile, for the incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״הִיא הָעוֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא ו:ב: 'על מוקדה' is the big pile, and 'ואש המזבח תוקד בו' is the קטורת pile.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי get his third pile?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יוסי's source for the pile of קיום האש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי, where does he learn the pile for keeping the fire going?
steps.whatsHappening: With the shared two piles secured, the גמרא moves to the first disputed pile and asks for רבי יוסי's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי has one pile more than רבי יהודה. A pile on the מזבח needs a source in the תורה, so the גמרא asks where he finds it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?
The תנא who counts three piles daily and four on יום כיפור

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei,
the pile for keeping the fire going — from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, קִיּוּם הָאֵשׁ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the agreed piles to the first disputed pile.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי's verse for the קיום האש pile.

steps.title: רבי יוסי learns it from a third mention of fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns קיום האש from 'והאש על המזבח תוקד בו' (ויקרא ו:ה).
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'And the fire on the מזבח shall be kept burning on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי uses a different verse a few פסוקים later, which mentions fire again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third mention of fire on the מזבח. רבי יוסי reads it as a third pile, whose job is to keep the fire alive.

keyTerms.meaning: ויקרא ו:ה, the third mention of fire

phrases.english: He derives it
from "And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it" (Leviticus 6:5).

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ: מִ״וְּהָאֵשׁ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ תּוּקַד בּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא ו:ה is the source for the קיום האש pile.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses that verse for lighting the kindling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not count a קיום האש pile, because he uses ויקרא ו:ה for the lighting of the kindling chips.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? That verse comes to teach about lighting the kindling chips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה does not learn a third pile from the same verse: he needs it for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an unspoken question: if the verse is there, why does רבי יהודה have only two piles? The answer is that he uses the verse for הצתת אליתא, the lighting of the thin chips that start the fire. So the verse is already used up for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin wood chips used as kindling

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
That verse comes to teach about lighting the kindling chips.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: הָהוּא, לְהַצָּתַת אֲלִיתָא הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the other side reads the verse that רבי יוסי used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses ויקרא ו:ה for הצתת אליתא, not for a pile.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows both readings of the verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יהודה learns from the verse that the kindling must be lit on top of the מזבח, while רבי יוסי learns the קיום האש pile from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה would say: from where do we know that the kindling chips may be lit only on top of the מזבח? The verse says, 'And the fire on the מזבח shall be kept burning on it.' רבי יוסי said: from where do we know that one makes a pile for keeping the fire going? The verse says, 'And the fire on the מזבח shall be kept burning on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי really read the same verse in these two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'על המזבח' teaches where the lighting happens: on top of the מזבח, not below with the fire carried up. For רבי יוסי, the same words teach an extra pile. The ברייתא confirms what the גמרא said in Steps 20–21.
steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים quote the exact same words of the פסוק. Their disagreement is only about what those words teach, not about which verse it is.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda would say:
From where do we know about lighting the kindling chips

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אֶלָּא בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ?
phrases.english: that it may be done only on top of the altar?
The verse teaches:
"And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it."
Rabbi Yosei said:
From where do we know that one makes a pile for keeping the fire going?
The verse teaches:
"And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Steps 20–21 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה reads ויקרא ו:ה as הצתת אליתא and רבי יוסי reads it as קיום האש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting both תנאים on the same verse.

steps.title: Then where does רבי יוסי learn the kindling law?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי used the verse for קיום האש, the גמרא asks where he learns that the kindling is lit on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי, where does he learn the law of lighting the kindling chips?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question flips to the other side. רבי יוסי used up the verse, so where does he get the rule about lighting the kindling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes רבי יוסי agrees that the kindling must be lit on top of the מזבח. Since he already used ויקרא ו:ה for his extra pile, he needs a different source for this rule.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei,
the lighting of the kindling chips — from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, הַצָּתַת אֲלִיתָא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question: now רבי יוסי needs a source for the law רבי יהודה learned from the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי's source for הצתת אליתא on top of the מזבח.

steps.title: He learns it from where רבי שמעון does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns הצתת אליתא from the same source as רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the same place that רבי שמעון learns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly and points to רבי שמעון's source. It will show that source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of quoting a verse right away, the גמרא links רבי יוסי to a known reading of רבי שמעון. That reading appears in the ברייתא that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose reading רבי יוסי follows

phrases.english: He derives it from the place
from which Rabbi Shimon derives it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהֵיכָא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 and sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי uses רבי שמעון's source.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads 'the sons of Aharon' as requiring a fit כהן
steps.stepSummary: In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה learns from 'ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש' that the kindling must be lit by a fit כהן with a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the sons of Aharon the כהן shall put fire on the מזבח.' This teaches that the lighting of the kindling chips must be done only by a fit כהן and with a service vessel. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that contains רבי שמעון's source. It opens with רבי יהודה's reading of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the words 'בני אהרן הכהן' teach who must do the lighting: a fit כהן, using a כלי שרת. This sets up רבי שמעון's argument in the next step, which gives the verse a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who is fit for service
A vessel used for Temple service
The words of (introduces whose view it is)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put
fire on the altar" (Leviticus 1:7) —
this teaches about lighting the kindling chips
that it may be done only by a fit priest
and with a service vessel,
phrases.notes: Sefaria translates this as 'in the priestly vestments of service' (reading בגדי שרת).

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אֵשׁ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא that Step 24 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: Shows where רבי שמעון's reading comes from, starting with the view he will argue against.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the verse teaches lighting on top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that it is obvious a non-כהן cannot approach the מזבח, so the verse must teach that the kindling is lit on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: Could it enter your mind that a non-כהן may come near the מזבח? Rather, the verse teaches that the lighting of the kindling chips must be done only on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון rejects רבי יהודה's reading. A verse is not needed to tell us that a זר cannot serve at the מזבח, so the verse must be teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic: a פסוק should not be used to teach something already obvious. Since 'only a כהן' is obvious, רבי שמעון reads 'אש על המזבח' as teaching the place of the lighting: on top of the מזבח. This is the source רבי יוסי uses, which frees ויקרא ו:ה for his קיום האש pile.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: Two laws come from two verses, and each pair of תנאים splits them differently. רבי יהודה: ויקרא ו:ה teaches that the kindling is lit on top of the מזבח, so he has no קיום האש pile; ויקרא א:ז teaches that a fit כהן must do it. רבי יוסי (following רבי שמעון): ויקרא א:ז teaches that the kindling is lit on top of the מזבח, which frees ויקרא ו:ה to teach the קיום האש pile.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a disagreement about the number of wood piles depends on how each תנא spends a limited set of verses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
Could it enter your mind
that a non-priest may approach the altar?
Rather, it teaches about lighting the kindling chips

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אֶלָּא בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: that it may be done only on top of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וְכִי תַּעֲלֶה עַל דַּעְתְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's reading within the same ברייתא and gives the reading רבי יוסי follows.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading ויקרא א:ז as requiring a כהן for the lighting.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is obvious that a זר may not approach the מזבח, so a verse is not needed for that.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains why the verse is still needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers רבי שמעון's objection. If we only knew the rule from the general ban on a non-כהן approaching the מזבח, we might think a non-כהן could stand on the ground and fan the fire with a bellows. So the verse is needed to teach that only a כהן may kindle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי יהודה respond? If we learned it only from there, I would have said a non-כהן may stand on the ground and work with a bellows. The verse teaches us that this is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה against רבי שמעון's claim that the verse would be teaching something obvious. It shows that the verse teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that a non-כהן obviously cannot go up to the מזבח, so the verse cannot be teaching that. רבי יהודה replies that the general ban only covers going up onto the מזבח. A non-כהן standing below and fanning the flames with a bellows would not be going up at all. The verse 'ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש' teaches that even this indirect kindling must be done by a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: If we learned it from there (from the other source alone)
I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
A bellows, used to fan a fire

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'הֲוָה אָמֵינָא' introduces a mistaken idea that the verse comes to reject. It is not רבי יהודה's actual view. He is saying 'without the verse, I might have thought this.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The question is: how does רבי יהודה answer רבי שמעון's objection?

phrases.english: If from there, I would have said:
he stands on the ground and works with a bellows,
phrases.notes: This refers to a non-priest fanning the altar fire from below.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אִי מֵהָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's objection from step 26 and defends רבי יהודה's reading from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verse is not superfluous because it adds a new case: indirect kindling from the ground.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the verse, a non-כהן could kindle the fire from the ground using a bellows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse requires that a כהן do the kindling in every way, even indirectly.

steps.title: Where does רבי מאיר learn the extra pile for leftover limbs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's source for a separate מערכה for limbs and fats that did not finish burning from the previous evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: the limbs and fats that were not consumed from the evening, where does he learn them from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי מאיר, who counts an extra מערכה for leftover pieces. It asks what verse that extra pile comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds there are more מערכות than רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה do. One of his extra piles is for limbs and fats left unburned overnight. Since every pile needs a source, the גמרא asks where this one is learned.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs of the עולה offering burned on the מזבח
Fats of the offerings burned on the מזבח
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
limbs and fats that were not consumed from the evening,
from where does he derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי to רבי מאיר's extra מערכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source for רבי מאיר's separate מערכה for leftover אברים ופדרים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns it from the extra letter 'and'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns the extra מערכה from the word 'וְאֵשׁ'. The extra ו ('and') hints at one more pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from 'and the fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר finds his source in the letter ו at the start of the word 'וְאֵשׁ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said 'אֵשׁ' (fire). The added ו ('and') means 'something more', which רבי מאיר reads as one more מערכה. That pile is the one for the leftover limbs and fats.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (literally: it comes out to him)
'And the fire', the word with the extra ו

phrases.english: He derives it from: 'and the fire.'
phrases.notes: The extra letter ו ('and') adds another fire pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו of 'וְאֵשׁ' teaches an added מערכה.

steps.title: The רבנן do not expound the letter ו ('and')
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן (רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה) do not learn anything from an extra ו. That is why they have no extra pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן do not expound the letter ו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר. They simply do not learn laws from an extra ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the disagreement depends on a method of reading verses, not on logic about the fire. רבי מאיר treats an extra ו as meaningful. The רבנן treat it as a normal part of the language, so for them no extra pile comes out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; here, רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה
They do not expound (learn laws from) the letter ו

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's extra מערכה for leftover limbs comes from the ו in 'וְאֵשׁ'. The רבנן don't expound the ו, so they don't have this pile.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis do not expound the vav.

steps.triggerLanguage: וָאו לָא דָּרְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the other side does not accept the derivation of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן reject the derivation because they don't expound an extra ו.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the leftover limbs?
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן have no special pile for the leftover limbs and fats, the גמרא asks what happens to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, the limbs and fats not consumed from the evening, what do they do with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up question. Without a special pile, where do the leftover pieces get burned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover pieces still have to finish burning; that much is not in doubt. The question is only where this happens according to the רבנן, since they have no extra מערכה for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with them?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
limbs and fats that were not consumed from the evening
what do they do with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי עָבֵיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 30: if the רבנן have no extra pile, what is their practice?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the רבנן burn the leftover אברים ופדרים.

steps.title: The leftovers go back to the large pile
steps.stepSummary: The כהן puts the leftover limbs and fats back onto the מערכה גדולה (the large main fire pile) so they finish burning there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He returns them to the large מערכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן place the leftovers back on the main fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן don't need a separate pile, because the large מערכה can finish burning the leftovers. This shows that both sides agree the leftovers must be burned. They only argue about whether this requires its own pile.

keyTerms.meaning: The large main fire pile on the מזבח

phrases.english: He returns them to the large arrangement.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהְדַּר לְהוּ לְמַעֲרָכָה גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leftovers are put back on the מערכה גדולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins as the source for returning the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that asks for the source for leftover limbs and fats. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that limbs and fats that were not consumed from the evening…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to support the answer it just gave, and the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דְּתַנְיָא' tells us a supporting source is coming. So far we have only the ברייתא's question about leftover limbs and fats. Its answer, which supports returning them to the large מערכה, follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught:
From where do we know regarding limbs and fats
that were not consumed from the evening
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer of step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That according to the רבנן the leftover אברים ופדרים are returned to the מערכה גדולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא beginning 'מנין לאיברים ופדרים שלא נתעכלו מבערב' (it continues on the next amud).
